findings.issue: earlier_attempt_commits proves only that the recorded start head is an object git holds (rev-parse --verify), not that it is an ancestor of HEAD. After a rebase or reset that leaves the old head in the object store, start..HEAD lists every commit since the merge base that touches a declared file, and the `others` filter (other tasks' recorded commit SHAs) is stale for the same reason. The refusal then tells the person to close on a sha that is not the attempt's. This cannot make the close ACCEPT anything (the refusal gate is unchanged: only the last sentence differs, and `done --commit` re-verifies in audit-task.py), so it is wrong advice, not a loosened guard.
findings.resolution: Add `git merge-base --is-ancestor <start_head> HEAD` beside the rev-parse and return ([], "") when it is not, so the old advice is given when no honest span exists.

findings.issue: start_head_of is a second copy of audit-task._start_head (same journal scan, same taskId/attempt/commit match, same hex-shape test). Two readers of one row shape will drift; the module layering here already shares _journal_io, so the scan itself could live in one place.
findings.resolution: Have audit-task._start_head call _scoped_commit.start_head_of (or move both to _journal_io) with the rows it already reads.

findings.issue: _stream_subprocess writes and closes the child's stdin outside the try/finally. The comment 'a verb reads its stdin before it prints, so the pipe never fills' does not cover a verb that exits before reading stdin (an argparse refusal or a bad manifest path). The close then raises BrokenPipeError, which escapes with the child unreaped and its stdout pipe open, in a path that is meant to report 'its own lines above say what it refused' rather than crash learning.
findings.resolution: Wrap the write/close in `try/except (BrokenPipeError, OSError): pass` (as subprocess.communicate does) and keep the wait/stdout drain in the existing finally.

findings.issue: case_binding_unchecked's sentences go only to ctx['did'] (the drive's run log); body[GAPS_FIELD] and the filed return carry only the graded gaps. Acceptance (1) asks that B's ids be 'reported as not checked', but the reviewer's brief prints the filed testsAddGaps, so an id that was never compared with a printed label reads as clean there. The ungraded ids are therefore invisible where the next judge looks.
findings.resolution: File the unchecked sentences in the return beside GAPS_FIELD (a second field the brief prints) or append them to the gaps list under a distinct 'not checked' wording the brief already renders.

findings.issue: The lint's name resolution is file-wide, not scope-wide: _constant_names collects every string assigned to a name anywhere in the file. Probed on the new code: `x = "--text"` at module level plus `def r(b): x = b; return [x, b]` reports 'line 4: --text' although x holds a built value there. Likewise `T = "a"` then `["--text", T]` is reported because a Name is not an ast.Constant, though the value is a literal. mt8 only checks the opposite scoping (separate lists), so neither over-fire is pinned.
findings.resolution: Resolve a Name against the assignments of its own function (fall back to the module only for names never assigned locally), treat a Name bound only to string constants as a literal value, and add both as ALLOW cases next to mt8.

findings.issue: The (c) fix is a runtime rewrite that knows ONE flag (`_STDIN_TEXT_FLAG = "--description"`) and moves only its first occurrence; the lint that would catch the class is run over drive-phase.py alone (test_drive_phase.py:7565). Probed: the new lint reports full-gate.py line 406 (`--description`, _described(...)) as a violation, so the class stays open here - a second built prose flag added to a full-gate verb argv (e.g. --reason) goes on argv unnoticed, and stdin carries only one flag per call.
findings.resolution: Either run argv_prose_violations over full-gate.py with the call-site exempted by name, or derive the flag from the verb's PROSE_FLAGS like the lint does and refuse (not silently pass on argv) a verb argv holding a second built prose flag.
